records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — [P2, confidence 75, advisory] Calling "OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)" before Upload.create_for and without a server-side multipart input-size or conversion-time limit lets a logged-in client submit an oversized image directly and occupy shared upload workers with up to five conversion subprocesses even when conversion fails and upload validation subsequently rejects it; the strongest rebuttal is the 10 MB cap and five-attempt bound, but that cap covers only browser validation and URL downloads, and the attempt bound limits neither input size nor the cost of one conversion.
records.rationale: The diff shows a new while loop at lines 63-67 in uploads_controller.rb that calls OptimizedImage.downsize up to 5 times. Looking at the downsize method in optimized_image.rb, it calls optimize() which eventually runs `convert_with(instructions, to)` that executes a shell command via backticks without any timeout mechanism. The finding correctly identifies that these subprocess calls have no timeout, and if a conversion hangs, it would block the worker. This is a real defect in the newly introduced code.
